exposure: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) (preeclampsia, eclampsia, gestational hypertension)
outcome: Maternal cardiac complications (arrhythmia, pulmonary edema, myocardial ischemia, heart failure, hemodynamic instability)
cohort: The study reviewed medical records of 250 women aged 18-45 years with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy who underwent cesarean section.
finding: Maternal cardiac complications are common in women with HDP undergoing cesarean section, and invasive intraoperative hemodynamic monitoring significantly reduced the likelihood of undetected hemodynamic deterioration.
mod_finding: General anesthesia during cesarean section was independently associated with an increased cardiac risk for women with HDP.
